instruction: Turn on gzip for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON and SVG responses with a vary header for caches.
Set a gzip minimum length of 1 KB, compression level 6 and a 4x16k buffer for text-heavy pages.
Compress JSON responses from the REST API behind a CDN, varying on accept-encoding.
Enable gzip but skip the ancient Internet Explorer 6 user agent.
Compress proxied responses only when the client sent no-cache, no-store or private directives.
Serve precompressed .gz files next to the originals for the static marketing site.
Use the maximum gzip compression level 9 for the text-only knowledge base site.
Use gzip compression level 1 with a 4 KB minimum size on the low-CPU edge server that serves many concurrent users.
Compress only the classic trio of HTML, CSS and JavaScript on the company brochure site.
Enable gzip globally for one virtual host only, leaving other server blocks uncompressed.
Compress everything served from the /assets/ directory of the storefront.
Only gzip for HTTP/1.1 clients and advertise the compressed variant to caches.
Compress proxied responses from the microservice fleet with a generous buffer size.
Keep gzip enabled for the HTTPS vhost of the news portal so CDNs store one compressed variant.
Disable gzip for the /downloads/ location that already stores compressed archives.
Compress RSS and Atom feeds along with plain HTML for the blog.
Compress SVG illustrations and the web app manifest for the design system site.
Compress CSV and TSV report exports served by the analytics dashboard.
Compress JavaScript source maps and worker scripts for the developer portal.
Configure a complete production gzip profile in the http block: on, level 6, 256 byte minimum, vary, proxied and IE6 excluded.
